awakening-tide.title: Awakening on the Tide
awakening-tide.text: You are sitting on a horse, chest-deep in warm dark water under a bruised violet sky. There is no horizon — sea and sky bleed into the same colour somewhere far off. A gull cries the same three notes, again, and again, and again. Something about this is wrong.

choices.label: Look at your hands
Ask the horse its name
Ignore it, ride for the horizon

first-reality-check.title: First Reality Check
first-reality-check.text: You look at your hands. The fingers ripple like reflections on water, and for a moment there are six of them, then five again. It clicks: this is a dream, and you are awake inside it. The realisation is the whole trick — reality checks work because you actually look, and actually ask.

choices.label: Stabilize the dream first — rub your palms, name what you see
Don't wait — try to fly right now
Ask the horse to guide you

the-horse-speaks.title: The Horse Speaks
the-horse-speaks.text: The horse turns its head further than a neck should turn and answers you in a voice that isn't quite a voice — more like a thought wearing sound. What it says is cryptic, half a riddle, half a memory that isn't yours. Dream characters rarely hand you the answer outright; they reflect back whatever you already half-know.

choices.label: Ask directly: "am I dreaming?"
Ride on without pressing further

denial-drift.title: Denial Drift
denial-drift.text: You push the thought away and ride on. The water thickens like syrup. The same gull crosses the same patch of sky on the same three notes, and your reflection lags half a second behind you now. Dream signs don't go away when ignored — they stack, louder, until they're impossible not to notice.

choices.label: Fine — really look this time
Keep riding, trust it's real

evasive-answer.title: An Evasive Answer
evasive-answer.text: Whatever the horse said dissolves into wind before it finishes. Its mane flickers to smoke for half a heartbeat, then settles back to hair. Nothing was confirmed outright — but a seed is planted, and dream logic rewards a second question more than a first.

choices.label: Press it again
Let it go, follow the light on the water

horse-as-guide.title: The Horse as Guide
horse-as-guide.text: Instead of forcing anything, you ask the dream itself for help. The horse breaks into a gallop across water that now holds like glass underfoot. Ahead, a figure in a long coat stands perfectly still on the waves — someone, or something, the dream has made to meet you.

choices.label: Approach the figure
Steer away and explore alone

stable-lucidity.title: Stable Lucidity
stable-lucidity.text: You rub your palms together and name three things you can see. The scene sharpens — colours saturate, the water's texture resolves into something you could almost count grain by grain. This is what a stabilized lucid dream feels like: fragile agency turned into something you can actually use.

choices.label: Fly out over the sea
Dive beneath the water
Seek out the dream's other inhabitants

wobbling-dream.title: A Wobbling Dream
wobbling-dream.text: The stabilization fumbles. Colour drains from the edges of the scene and the horizon starts to pixelate, the way a dream does right before it collapses. This is recoverable — a decaying dream is a warning, not a verdict.

choices.label: Grab the reins hard, ground yourself in touch
Let it collapse, see where you land

flight-over-sea.title: Flight Over the Sea
flight-over-sea.text: You lift off the horse's back into open air, the endless sea unrolling beneath you. Flying is the classic impossible-physics dream sign — and doing it on purpose, instead of stumbling into it, is most of the lesson.

choices.label: Fly toward the storm on the horizon
Land on the water and walk on it

fall-through-water.title: Falling Through Water
fall-through-water.text: The flight fails — you drop instead of rise — but the sea receives you gently and you keep sinking, slow as a held breath. In a lucid dream, failure is rarely a dead end. It's just a different door than the one you tried.

choices.label: Breathe underwater on purpose
Swim for the surface

the-waveborn-guide.title: The Waveborn Guide
the-waveborn-guide.text: Up close, the coated figure's face keeps almost resolving into someone you know, then sliding away from it. It offers you a small, plain question about the sea — the kind of test dream characters pose that ends up mirroring a doubt you already carry awake.

choices.label: Answer honestly, whatever comes to mind
Refuse to play along, walk past

beneath-the-waves.title: Beneath the Waves
beneath-the-waves.text: Under the surface, the "sea" turns out to be an inverted sky — stars strung out beneath you instead of above. Nobody sent you here to solve anything. This is just what's on the other side of curiosity, and it's reason enough on its own.

choices.label: Rise back up toward the storm
Let yourself wake

the-storm-eye.title: The Eye of the Storm
the-storm-eye.text: The storm on the horizon is perfectly still at its centre. Standing in that stillness, riderless, is the horse — waiting exactly the way it was waiting at the very start. The dream is folding back on itself, and for the first time you can see the seam.

choices.label: Mount the horse again
Refuse — hold your ground in the eye of the storm

light-on-water.title: A Light on the Water
light-on-water.text: A small warm light drifts on the water ahead, steady where everything else flickers. It doesn't ask anything of you. Dreamers who keep a journal by the bed describe this feeling on waking — the one clear thing worth writing down before the rest dissolves.

choices.label: Follow the light
Turn back to the horse's question

false-awakening-a.title: False Awakening (I)
false-awakening-a.text: You wake up — sitting on a horse, chest-deep in warm dark water, under a bruised violet sky. Nothing has changed. That, itself, is the tell: a false awakening looks exactly like relief, right up until you notice it isn't one.

choices.label: Recognize it for what it is

false-awakening-b.title: False Awakening (II)
false-awakening-b.text: You wake with a jolt, certain you're back in your own bed — until you notice the reins still looped around your hand, and the same gull, still singing its three notes through a window that shouldn't be there.

choices.label: Recognize it for what it is

lucid-mastery.title: The Eye Holds
lucid-mastery.text: For one suspended moment, the loop doesn't reset. You stay in the eye of the storm, fully lucid, fully aware that this exact dreamscape has come around before — and that noticing the repeat is the real skill, more than anything you did with the horse or the sea. That recognition is what carries over when you wake for real.
